verdicts.threatModel: No attacker is modelled by this rule: an `import SwiftUI` statement is a compile-time module reference in a first-party iOS app scaffold, not a data flow from any untrusted source to a sink.
verdicts.reachability: The import has no runtime input. ios/project.yml declares deploymentTarget iOS 17.0 and the Ember target `platform: iOS`; Info.plist sets LSRequiresIPhoneOS true, so the SwiftUI APIs used (NavigationStack, ContentUnavailableView, @Observable environment, fileImporter) are confirmed available on the declared platform target.
verdicts.impact: None. The rule asks only for platform-target confirmation, which project.yml supplies; the five member files (EditView, SettingsView, RootView, LibraryView, EmberApp) contain only static SwiftUI view composition with no trust boundary, so no confidentiality, integrity or availability impact exists.
verdicts.rationale: Platform target is confirmed by ios/project.yml lines 11-12 (`deploymentTarget: iOS: "17.0"`) and line 29 (`platform: iOS`); every SwiftUI API in the cluster is available at iOS 17, so the candidate is a provable non-issue.
